title: Rounding of the Standing Transfer Instalment by the Age of the Account
content:
How the instalment for a standing monthly transfer into an account of Savings & Money Market Accounts is rounded follows the age of the account, measured in whole months it has been open.

Where the account has been open no more than 12 whole months, the instalment is rounded half up to the whole dollar. Where it has been open more than 12 whole months but no more than 36 whole months, the instalment is truncated to the whole dollar. Where it has been open more than 36 whole months, the instalment is rounded half up to the cent.

### The same instalment under each rule

Take a hypothetical instalment of 166.6666 USD.

| Whole months the account has been open | Rounding applied | Figure |
| --- | --- | --- |
| no more than 12 | half up to the whole dollar | 167.00 USD |
| more than 12, no more than 36 | truncated to the whole dollar | 166.00 USD |
| more than 36 | half up to the cent | 166.67 USD |

Truncation to the whole dollar discards the cents rather than rounding them, so an instalment of 166.9900 USD becomes 166.00 USD on an account of 20 whole months, while the same figure becomes 167.00 USD on an account of 8 whole months and 166.99 USD on an account of 50 whole months.

### Boundary of the age

An account open exactly 12 whole months is rounded half up to the whole dollar; at 13 whole months it is truncated to the whole dollar. An account open exactly 36 whole months is still truncated to the whole dollar; at 37 whole months it is rounded half up to the cent.
